findings.title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` inside `errgroup.Go`
findings.body:
Inside the `for _, info := range stats` loop in `s.init`, the goroutines launched via `group.Go` mutate two outer-scope variables without synchronization:

1. `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the outer `err` variable (declared at line 181), rather than a goroutine-local `err`. When `s.initWorkers > 1`, multiple goroutines concurrently write to and read from `err`, causing a data race and potentially returning another goroutine's value.
2. `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) is also incremented concurrently without synchronization or atomic operations.

Before this PR, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire duration, which largely serialized the goroutines after `s.builders.get`. Removing that coarse lock in `bleve.go` now exposes this race whenever `s.initWorkers > 1`. Use `_, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`) for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

findings.title: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu`
findings.body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without holding `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. If `TotalDocs()` is called concurrently with `BuildIndex` (for example via `getOrCreateIndex` triggered by a `Search` request or watch event while another call is reading `TotalDocs()`), Go will panic with `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write`. Acquire `b.cacheMu.RLock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()` in `TotalDocs()`.

findings.title: Removing coarse lock in `BuildIndex` allows concurrent builds for the same key to collide or overwrite each other
findings.body:
Previously, `BuildIndex` locked `b.cacheMu` for the entire build. With the lock moved to only cover `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end of `BuildIndex`, two concurrent callers to `getOrCreateIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g., two concurrent `Search` requests for an unindexed namespace or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent`) will both see a cache miss in `GetIndex` and run `BuildIndex` concurrently.

- For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` call on the same directory will fail because the directory/boltdb lock already exists.
- For in-memory indexes, both will build separate `bleve.Index` instances, double-increment `IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` and `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds`, and the second will overwrite `b.cache[key]` without closing the first index.

Consider synchronizing builds per key (e.g., `singleflight` or a per-key lock) or re-checking `b.cache[key]` before building.

findings.title: `NewResourceServer` leaks the watch context and blob bucket if `s.Init` fails
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` creates a cancelable context (`ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` at line 229) and optionally opens a blob `bucket` (line 208), and now calls `s.Init(ctx)` at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` (or closing `bucket`), leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization (such as the watcher goroutine started by `s.search.init` if `s.initWatcher()` fails afterward). Call `cancel()` on the error path before returning.
